body:
Not a solution but a workaround:
- Have an event bus autoload with a level_loaded signal for the client
- In your game’s main scene root (multiplayer.gd in the case of the tutorial), on the client’s end,  have a function connected to multiplayer.connected_to_sever that makes a loading screen visible.
- Have a hide loading screen function connected to LocalClientEvents.level_loaded that hides the loading screen.
- in level.gd’s ready, if not multiplayer.is_server then emit the LocalClientEvents.level_loaded signal which hides the loading screen.

It’s obviously a bandaid suggestion and the loading screen would be generic/random with no bar at this stage - or just the ye ol ambiguous spinning circle since we don’t have any status on the resource loader nor know what resource to refer to to begin with on the client’s end.

I don’t know if it would work well but perhaps using a manual handshake udp packet with the server to obtain the level’s resource path, loading the level resource on the client’s end with a loading screen and THEN actually creating a client peer to actually have the spawner instantiate the level on the client’s end could work too.

Again, bandaid workarounds and I’m not an expert but if they somewhat hide the hanging I hope it helps!

The only workaround for this issue is:
1. By default set you Synchronizers `public_visibility` to Off. 
2. Upon `peer_connected` signal triggered, do RPC to the newly joined client to ask it to change scene to be in the same scene as the host(This is where you can roll our own loading solution).
3. Do a server RPC to acknowledge that the client is ready to reconcile with server.
4. The server `set_visibility_for(client, true)` to synchronize with clients.

This whole flow is very tedious, finicky and will not work properly if your game is based around client authority. Hopefully, Godot will have a solution for it in the future.
